charts.title: Traffic split matches the intended 96/4 (Ads 96.0%, PSA 4.0%): no sample ratio mismatch
charts.subtitle: Share of users by group vs the intended 96/4 split (dashed line)
takeaways: PSA has 23,524 users vs 23,524 expected under 96/4
Chi-square p = 1.000 (threshold 0.001): the split is as intended
The first-stated 95/5 split failed (p < 0.001); the user confirmed 96/4
charts.source: Source: marketing_AB.csv (test dates not recorded); n = 588,101 users; chi-square goodness-of-fit test
charts.notes: speaker note: the groups are the size they were meant to be, so the comparison can be trusted on this check.

charts.title: Ads lift conversion by +43.1% vs PSA, statistically significant and above the 5% practical threshold
charts.subtitle: Relative lift in conversion vs PSA; z-test 95% CI, Bayesian 95% credible interval
takeaways: Even the low end (+29.3%) is above the 5% practical threshold
charts.source: Source: marketing_AB.csv (test dates not recorded); n = 588,101 users; two-proportion z-test and beta-binomial model
charts.notes: speaker note: the headline - ads clearly raise conversion, by far more than the bar we set.

charts.title: Ads users convert at 2.55% vs 1.79% with PSA: 7.7 extra conversions per 1,000 users, significant
charts.subtitle: Conversion rate by group, 95% CI
takeaways: Difference +0.77 pp: 7.7 extra per 1,000 users (95% CI 6.0 to 9.4)
charts.source: Source: marketing_AB.csv (test dates not recorded); n = 588,101 users; two-proportion z-test
charts.notes: speaker note: in plain terms, roughly eight more conversions for every thousand people who see the ads.

charts.title: Plausible conversion rates for Ads and PSA do not overlap: Ads beat PSA with > 99.9% probability
charts.subtitle: Posterior distribution of the conversion rate by group; label = posterior mean
takeaways: The ranges are fully separated; the flat prior carries negligible weight at this sample size
charts.source: Source: marketing_AB.csv (test dates not recorded); beta-binomial model, Beta(1, 1) prior; n = 588,101 users
charts.notes: speaker note: the Ads curve sits entirely to the right of the PSA curve - no plausible world where PSA wins.

charts.title: Ads beat PSA on conversion with > 99.9% probability, above the 95% decision threshold
charts.subtitle: Posterior probability that Ads convert better than PSA
takeaways: P(Ads beat PSA) > 99.9% vs a 95% decision threshold
Staying with PSA would cost an expected 0.77 pp of conversion
charts.source: Source: marketing_AB.csv (test dates not recorded); beta-binomial model, Beta(1, 1) prior; n = 588,101 users
charts.notes: speaker note: the Bayesian decision rule says ship - the chance ads are worse than PSA is negligible.

charts.title: Exploratory, not causal: lift significant only at 21-50, 51-100 and 101-200 ads seen; 4 of 7 buckets inconclusive
charts.subtitle: Relative conversion lift, Ads vs PSA, by ads seen, 95% CI. Ads seen is measured during the test, not assigned
charts.key_message: Exploratory: lift significant in 3 of 7 ads-seen buckets (not causal)
takeaways: Inconclusive: 1-5, 6-10, 11-20 and 201+ ads - wide intervals, not no effect
Ads seen reflects behaviour; PSA share varies by bucket (p < 0.001): not dose-response
charts.source: Source: marketing_AB.csv (no dates); z-test per bucket, Benjamini-Hochberg across 7 buckets; n = 588,101 users
charts.notes: speaker note: descriptive only - heavier-exposure users are different people, so this does not show that more ads cause more lift.
